title: The Philippines.
body:
O.P.
Hey there. Noticing that the Philippines appears to open, with the only requirement being a supervised RAT test before departure, for vaccinated travelers. I was thinking about Thailand, but as it stands, due to only having two weeks, I consider Thailand too big a risk. For example, mandatory quarantine in a hotel, whilst one awaits for a result of a PCR test. Then a RAT test on day five..note I have had COVID and am concerned that with the PCR test Thailand uses it may show positive. With quarantine at your expense if you test positive. Rumour has it that this may all change on May the 1st. With this in mind, the Phills has come top on mind. Havent been there in many years, however it was a great stopoff back in the day, I got to explore Manila and its environs. Anyone with recent experience travelling there? I was thinking Boracay, Palawan, a chilled holiday. If you have, how did you find travel within the Phils? I have heard of paperwork before going to Boracay etc...from Manila. Or do you have recommendations on what to see, visit.

---- replies ----
[User #55240613880 postscreampuffWhirlpool Forums Addict] If you go to Boracay or Palawan, you are almost certainly going to have to take a domestic flight (the only other alternative is inter island ferry). Just pointing this out as you refer to Manila and environs.
[User #8692625 postsWooinsert humour here...Whirlpool Enthusiast] Either or both is a good choice. I have friend that has visited both recently and I'm back in the Philippines myself next week (I was there in Feb/Mar too). The Philippines is recovering from its shutdown. Although Boracay is getting busy again, a lot of shops are still shut. There's some recovery still to do. Also consider Siargao Island and there are many other spots that are smaller, but have great little adventures, such as Malapascua Island off the northern coast of Cebu. It all depends on what you're seeking :)
[User #689041851 postsMaxwellbestWhirlpool Enthusiast] O.P.
Thanks Woo...seeking perhaps a wee bit of nightlife (Manila) then some adventure, chill seeking. Those places you mentioned could be just the thing...
[User #8609783669 postsDave.KWhirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
I'm in Philippines now, they were surprisingly quick at getting us through. The only difference to arrival procedure is that they scan you One health pass qr code prior to immigration.
The only thing that is different is that hotels ask for your vaccination certificate and mask everywhere requiment which, outside isn't nice in the tropical weather. Thankfully the scuba diving place I'm at in Mabini are casual about it.
I'm told Palawan and Boracay still has entry processes with Spass, etc but around Luzon, Batangas you can move unimpeded by anything other than traffic. Nasugbu is accessible from Manila and has some nice beach front resorts if Palawan/Borocay is too hard to get to.
[User #280851951 postsJimbyWhirlpool Enthusiast] Hot Monster writes...
Chocolate hills.
Well you could go to Albay province/ Legazpi where they have the Green Hills that are very similar to the Chocolate Hills, they also have an underground river and the world marvel Mt Mayon. Top that with friendly people and a new Bicol International Airport and it's got stuff to offer. I can't talk about elseware however except Manila which is a good place to escape from.
[User #3819727625 postsMav_auWhirlpool Forums Addict] If you're going to go soon then watch out for the typhoons. Mid year sucks for non stop rain and floods.
[User #689041851 postsMaxwellbestWhirlpool Enthusiast] O.P.
Hmmm, yes did a check..seems Palawan should be OK in May, this is an impromptu visit, have gotten time off work so want to make the most of it. May I ask what covid insurance providers you guys used? Plus that Spass thing..hassle?
[User #8609783669 postsDave.KWhirlpool Forums Addict] Maxwellbest writes...
covid insurance providers you guys used? Plus that Spass thing..hassle?
We used RAA. The thing to watch out insurance wise is Philippines is a level 3 'reconsider travel' on smarttraveller.gov.au and some companies do not cover you for level 3 countries.
I forgot to mention that on arrival into Manila that no one checked that we had a insurance with US$35,000 covid medical coverage.
We haven't done any Spass as the regions we are visiting are under level 1 restrictions and do not require use of Spass. There are some places with 'check points' but these existed pre covid. My wife got stopped by at one on the way to pick me up from diving at Anilao amd they just asked where she was going and let her through.
Getting around, in greater Manila region there is Grab (uber equivalent). To get to other places you can hire a car, there is the option of self drive or driver supplied. We're self driving. While traffic looks crazy sometimes it's easy to pick up on the 'flow'. In short, basically every one gives way, eg even if you are comming out from a side street, just start coming out and they will generally let you in. In the provence on multi lane roads, Jeeps and tricycles think they own the road and will sit in the centre lane doing 30km/h, just have to pass them on the right
[User #321659446 postsLiverpool_YNWAForum Regular] We've booked in to go over in December for a month. Hoping by then incoming tests won't be required. The government is under reporting covid numbers so they can still have election rallies.
[User #3819727625 postsMav_auWhirlpool Forums Addict] Yep and everyone in PH is suspecting once the elections are over it's going straight back into lockdown. It's ridiculous how they are squashing thousands of people together into the rallies like that.
[User #32574111872 postsHot MonsterWhirlpool Forums Addict] Philippines facts: 1. Open to tourists from Feb 2022 (2 months ago) 2. 100,000 tourists entered from 1 Feb to 15 Mar, only about 10% of the number before COVID 3. Most tourists are Filipino. 4. Flights and accommodation are expensive, more than what you would pay before COVID
[User #8609783669 postsDave.KWhirlpool Forums Addict] Liverpool_YNWA writes...
The government is under reporting covid numbers
This has been going on for months, I don't thing anyone believed a couple months back that a country of 110 million people had less than 1000 cases a day, less than South Australia. Testing for a long time wasn't free, so the choice was simple. Have money to eat for a month or blow a month's food budget on a test and potentially die starving with Covid.
Hot Monster writes...
4. Flights and accommodation are expensive, more than what you would pay before COVID Flights are a bit more expensive acreloss the board but outside of the peak easter/holidays they are within the range I've seen during high oil prices. I don't think low cost carriers like Cebu Pacific who run all economy A330s are operating yet. Qantas has only been operating from a fortnight before Easter. On our flight there was probably more filo's than average but I wasn't taking too much notice.
Hotel's have been mixed, but there are deals around, eg I've been able to find Dusit Thani and hotels in Alabang at within $10/night to pre covid rates,
[User #321659446 postsLiverpool_YNWAForum Regular] Ive found airfares and hotels to be cheaper than pre-Covid. Know your prices and you'll do well.
[User #321659446 postsLiverpool_YNWAForum Regular] btw if you have a filipino spouse the family doesn't have to satisfy the $35k covid medical coverage.
[User #3819727625 postsMav_auWhirlpool Forums Addict] Flights seemed about the same from gold coast. i'm going tomorrow morning with scoot, $178 to singapore then $100 to Manila, pretty much the same as pre covid.
